name: Ci Gbe
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Henson, Bonnie J. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo, Volume 6: Ci language area. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011-018. Dallas: SIL International. 45 pp. (downloaded via the Internet Archive id_ capture of the sil.org reapdata URL)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey only (interviews, Fon RA-RTT, lexicostatistics); 'stress' and 'tone' 0 hits; 'accent' only in the folk sense (sec. 6.1 p. 10: 'no dialects of Ci, although there are differences in accents from one village to another'). Sec. 2.1/3: Capo 1986/1991 mention Ci but leave it unclassified; SIL word lists put Ci in the Fon cluster; two of three Ci communities say they speak 'Kotafon'. References cite Tchitchi 1994 'Ce que parler ci veut dire' (CBRST).

sources.citation: Kluge, Angela. 2011. A sociolinguistic survey of the Gbe language communities of Benin and Togo: Gbe language family overview. SIL ESR 2011-012; and Kluge, Angela. 2008. The Gbe language varieties of West Africa: a quantitative analysis of lexical and grammatical features. SIL ESR 2008-023. (read held by the project in sibling folder gbes1238)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Classification only: Ci lexically groups with the Fon cluster; Capo 1986 map 2 marks Ci as a Fon variety, his official classification (1986:101) leaves it unclassified.

sources.citation: Gbeto, Flavien. 2006. La participation des consonnes comme unites porteuses de ton en kotafon, dialecte gbe du Sud-Benin. Journal of West African Languages 33(2): 87-107. (SISTER LECT Kotafon, kota1272 -- the name two of three Ci communities give their own speech; read held by the project in sibling folder ayiz1245)
sources.note: Kotafon, not Ci: two underlying tones H and B; derived M, BH, HB, MH, HM; intro p. 88 calls the HB melody imposed in verbal reduplication 'interpretation d'un phenomene accentuel'. No statement on word stress.

sources.citation: Tchitchi, Toussaint Yaovi. 2008. Le parler ci du continuum dialectal gbe: phonologie, elements de morphosyntaxe et de lexique thematique (Publication Labogbe no. 7). Garome/Cotonou: Labo Gbe / Les Editions Labo Gbe. 114 pp. ISBN 978-99919-69-72-5.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only primary phonological description of Ci Gbe located in any catalogue (LoC note: 'phonological sketch'); its phonology chapter is where any tone/stress/accent statement for Ci would be. Held BULAC Paris (SUDOC 144306786) and Library of Congress (LCCN 2011503019, PL8115.98.T35 2008).

sources.citation: Tchitchi, Toussaint Yaovi. 1994. Ce que parler ci veut dire. Cotonou: CBRST (Centre Beninois de la Recherche Scientifique et Technique).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Earlier Ci study by the same author, cited by Henson 2011; may contain a phonological sketch; not found in SUDOC/LoC/OpenLibrary/Glottolog.

sources.citation: Capo, Hounkpati B. C. 1991. A Comparative Phonology of Gbe (Publications in African Languages and Linguistics 14). Berlin/New York: Foris (de Gruyter); Garome: Labo Gbe. 238 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Family-wide phonology that mentions Ci (pp. xxiii, 3); its prosody/tone chapter is the standard Gbe-level statement (tonal; 'stress' indexed only for English loans p. 22). Would supply a family-level statement if no Ci-specific one exists.
sources.venue: Publications in African Languages and Linguistics 14

Etude comparative des parlers gbe du (Sud-)Benin, nos. 1-3 (Tchitchi; Hazoume; Capo, Approche phonologique segmentale). Cotonou: CENALA.
